--- title: "Get started" subtitle: "From event timing to an inspectable first-level fit." jupyter: python3 format: html: code-fold: false --- ## Install fmrimod is currently **alpha software**, requires Python **3.10 or newer**, and is not published on PyPI. Install the current source from GitHub with a supported interpreter: ```bash python3.11 -m venv .venv .venv/bin/python -m pip install "fmrimod @ git+https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/fmrimod.git" ``` For development from a clone, use the repository's uv-managed environment: ```bash uv venv --python 3.11 .venv uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python -e ".[dev,test,docs]" ``` ## Fit a small example Start with an event table and bind it to data in an `fmri_dataset`. The event table stores experimental timing; the dataset keeps data, TR, and events together. ::: {#1ecf6bbd .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import pandas as pd import fmrimod as fm from fmrimod.spec import compile as compile_spec from fmrimod.spec import hrf from fmrimod.contrast import condition from fmrimod.simulate import simulate_bold events = pd.DataFrame({ "onset": np.arange(8, 116, 12.0), "condition": "face", "duration": 2.0, }) ``` ::: `hrf(...)` describes the condition regressor. You can read its fields before compiling a design or fitting a model. ::: {#c092aff5 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} spec = hrf("condition", basis="spmg1") spec.variables, spec.hrf ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (('condition',), 'spmg1') ``` ::: ::: Generate a face-versus-baseline effect of `2.0` in two features and no effect in two others. This gives the fitted estimates something concrete to recover. ::: {#89af1927 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} sampling = fm.SamplingFrame(blocklens=130, TR=1.0) built, _ = compile_spec(spec, data=events, sampling_frame=sampling) bold = simulate_bold( np.asarray(built.design_matrix), np.array([[2.0, 2.0, 0.0, 0.0]]), noise_sd=0.3, n_voxels=4, rng=np.random.default_rng(7), ) dataset = fm.fmri_dataset(bold, tr=1.0, events=events) ``` ::: Fit the first-level model and ask for the face-versus-baseline contrast by condition name. With added noise, the estimates should be close to the injected effects. ::: {#d828dc83 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} fit = fm.fmri_lm(spec, dataset) faces = fit.contrast( condition("face", term="condition"), name="face_vs_baseline" ) pd.DataFrame({ "estimate": faces.estimate.round(3), "t": faces.stat.round(2), "p": faces.p_value.round(4), }) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
estimate t p
0 2.125 10.41 0.0000
1 2.352 11.97 0.0000
2 0.158 0.71 0.4790
3 0.188 0.85 0.3982
``` ::: ::: ## Inspect the design `fmri_lm()` built the design for you, and you can read it back from the fit. The columns first: ::: {#22f525a9 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} list(fit.model.design_matrix(run=0).columns) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ``` ['condition_condition.face', 'base_constant1_block_1'] ``` ::: ::: And the columns themselves. Each one is the condition's event timing convolved with the SPM canonical HRF, which is what `basis="spmg1"` in the spec selected: ::: {#752f420c .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} from fmrimod.visualization import plot_design_matrix # figsize is passed to the function, not set as a cell option: the plot # helper builds its own figure. fig, ax = plot_design_matrix(fit.model.event_model, figsize=(9, 3.2)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![The face-condition design regressor. Each event becomes one HRF response: a rise to peak around 5 s after onset, then an undershoot.](get-started_files/figure-html/cell-8-output-1.png){fig-alt='Line chart of the face-condition design regressor, with repeated hemodynamic peaks followed by shallow undershoots.'} ::: ::: Reading this plot is how you check a design before trusting a fit: each peak should follow an event, with the selected HRF's delay and undershoot. ::: {.callout-note collapse="true"} ## Coming from R / `fmrireg`? The R-style string formula still works and compiles to the *same* spec: `fm.fmri_lm("hrf(condition)", dataset)` is exact sugar for `fm.fmri_lm(hrf("condition"), dataset)`. Prefer the object form in Python: it composes with `+`, and your editor can introspect it before you fit. ::: ## Follow the result into a group model `fmri_dataset()` binds data to timing and events, `hrf(...)` is the design spec, `fmri_lm()` fits the public first-level path, and `fit.contrast(...)` states the hypothesis by name. This is the same sequence used in the worked tutorials: ```text fmri_dataset -> fmri_lm(spec) -> contrast -> group ``` The **[golden path](tutorials/golden-path.qmd)** runs this workflow from first-level estimates into a group model. It checks recovery on simulated data and explains a separate, checked-in Nilearn parity receipt. ## Next steps - [Tutorial: the golden path](tutorials/golden-path.qmd): the whole workflow, end to end - [Tutorial: real FIAC data](tutorials/real-data-fiac.qmd): the same modeling seam on neuroimaging data - [Concept: the modeling objects](concepts/mental-model.qmd): what each modeling value means - [Evidence and active caveats](evidence/index.qmd): what has been verified, and where it applies - [Tutorial: overview and workflow](tutorials/overview-workflow.qmd) - [Tutorial: design matrices](tutorials/design-matrices.qmd) - [Tutorial: linear model](tutorials/linear-model.qmd) - [Tutorial: contrasts](tutorials/contrasts.qmd) - [API reference](reference/index.qmd)
